app.title: Sync
tuto.title: Tutorial: set up a sync
tuto.intro: Two Grist documents on the same instance: the SOURCE sends tables, the TARGET receives an up-to-date copy. No data goes through the exchanged codes. Click a screenshot to enlarge it.
settings.title: Settings
settings.credits.author: Author
settings.diag.help: If something does not work, paste these diagnostics into your message: version, state of exports and receptions, recent errors. They contain none of your table data, no email, no code and no link.
common.readonly: Read only: an editor must open this page for actions to be available.
common.reloading: The widget’s access rules were updated: Grist is reloading the document…
send.ownersOnly: You are not an owner of this document: the list of exports and their recipients is reserved for its owners, so you cannot see it and cannot create anything here. To send tables from this document, ask one of them to open this page.
common.codeSecret: This code is as sensitive as a password: do not paste it into an AI, a ticket or a chat room. Give it directly to the person.
common.controlHelp: Compare it by phone with the other person, who sees the same one: a different code means the link was swapped on the way.
common.otherVersion: The other document uses version {theirs} of the widget (here: {mine}). If something fails, install the widget from the same address in both documents.
common.olderVersion: The other document uses a version of the widget older than 0.12 (here: {mine}). If something fails, install the widget from the same address in both documents.
home.title: What do you want to do in this document?
home.notOwner: You are not an owner of this document: sending tables is reserved for its owners, and receiving tables requires being an editor (a viewer sees the state but cannot act).
guide.title: Who does what?
guide.s1: Installs the widget, Send: creates an export (its tables and their columns), then “Add a recipient” and sends the invitation code to the TARGET.
guide.t1: Installs the widget, Receive, “Accept an invitation”: pastes the code, picks where each table goes.
guide.t2: Opens the form’s page, shown at the bottom of the page list: Share, Copy link. Pastes that link in the widget (one link for the whole export), then sends the reply code back to the SOURCE.
guide.s2: On the export card, invitation line: “Paste the reply”, checks who accepted, “Approve and connect”, then “Send” the existing rows.
guide.t3: Opens the widget page now and then: rows are copied into the tables while the page is open. A table added to the export later is offered there in a dialog.
guide.p.s1: Installs the widget, Send: creates an export, “Add a recipient”, Public link mode. Sends the code, then in Share, Manage users, sets “Public access” to On, as Viewer.
guide.p.t1: Installs the widget, Receive, “Accept an invitation”: pastes the code, picks the destinations. Reading happens while the page is open, every 10 seconds.
guide.e.s1: Installs the widget, Send: creates an export, “Add a recipient”, Exchange mode. Copies the link of the return form, published on its own page at the bottom of the page list, then sends the invitation code to the TARGET.
guide.e.t1: Installs the widget in a document they own, Receive, “Accept an invitation”: pastes the code, picks where each table goes.
guide.e.t3: Each document opens the widget page now and then: each copies, while the page is open, what the other changed. The most recent change wins.
guide.publicNote: In public link mode, one code is enough: the TARGET has no reply to send back.
guide.install: Install the widget: preferably from your instance’s widget gallery, if it is there. Otherwise: Add, Add page, Custom view, then Custom URL: paste the official address below (never another one), Add widget, and accept full access (Grist’s right panel, “Access level”: “Accept”).
guide.copyHandoff.help: The code and the other document’s steps, ready to paste in an email.
guide.handoff.target: Hello, I would like to share tables of my Grist document with you. In your Grist document (you need edit rights):
guide.handoff.source: Hello, here is my reply to your Grist sync invitation. In your document:
home.send.desc: This document is the SOURCE: its rows are copied into another document.
home.receive.desc: This document is the TARGET: it receives and maintains an editable copy.
send.empty: No export yet. An export groups tables and the chosen columns; you then add the people who receive it.
send.step.name: Name
send.tables.help: Tick the tables of the export.
send.edit.tables: Tick the tables of the export. An added table is offered to each recipient, who picks where it goes.
send.edit.removed: No longer sent: {tables}. What recipients already received stays with them.
send.columns.help: By default, all columns and all rows are sent. Narrow them down if needed: the rest never leaves the document. A Reference is sent as the text it shows.
send.columns.relay: Table received from another document: the widget relays it as received. Rows you add here by hand stay here, they are not sent.
send.columns.files: Attachments ({cols}): tick them to send them. Their files go out while an owner has this page open, 25 MB at most each.
send.links.help: A column that points at a row of another table of the export (Reference) becomes, on the receiving side, a real Reference to the received table, showing the same column. A column that already holds data there stays text.
send.lastOk: Last delivery dropped at the recipient: {at}. It shows in their table as soon as their widget page is open.
send.history.title: Send history ({n})
send.history.help: What the widget drove: resends, catch-ups, pauses, recipients. Ordinary sends leave from Grist: each recipient’s state tells whether they went through.
send.history.unblock: Send queue cleared, everything is sent again.
send.history.autopause: {who}: paused by the widget, its receiving link no longer worked.
send.paused.auto: Paused by the widget: its receiving link no longer worked (their document was deleted, the reception stopped, the link cut or the form unpublished: Grist answers the same in all four cases), and it was holding back deliveries to the other people of this document. Revoke them and invite them again; if the link is restored, resume their deliveries.
send.paused.slow: Paused by the widget: a send to this person was waiting for a reply that never came (Grist never gives up by itself), and it was holding back the sends to the other people of this document. If their document answers again, resume their sends; otherwise revoke them and invite them again.
send.backOptions.title: Back to the options?
send.backOptions.body: The current invitation is cancelled: its code will no longer work. You will create a new one, to send instead.
send.newCode.title: Make the invitation code again?
send.newCode.body: The widget keeps neither the code nor its secret: it makes a new one, and the old one will no longer work. Send the new one instead.
send.connected: Connected: additions, changes and deletions now go out on their own.
send.done: Existing rows sent: {n}. At the recipient they show up as soon as their widget page is open.
send.name: Export name
send.created.next: Now add the first person who receives it. From the export card, you can add others or revoke a single one.
send.edit.title: Edit “{name}”
send.edit.saved: Saved: {n} {n|row was|rows were} sent to the recipients.
send.filter.title: Rows of {table} to send
send.filter.none: No condition: all rows are sent.
send.filter.unreadable: Rows could not be read: no values or preview. Other conditions are still saved.
send.filter.nothing: No row will be sent: rows already sent will be deleted at the recipients.
send.filter.help: Only rows matching these conditions are sent (case does not matter). A Reference is chosen by its record: renamed, it stays in the filter. A row that leaves the filter is deleted at the recipients. The list of choices of a Choice column is not sent: each recipient only gets the values of the rows sent.
send.files.pending: {n} {n|file|files} to send: {n|it goes|they go} out while this page stays open.
send.export.lost: Table not found (renamed or deleted): {tables}. Its rows are no longer sent. Give it back its name, or remove it from the export (Edit).
send.export.drift: Columns changed since the export (renamed, deleted, of another type or hidden by an access rule): {cols}. They are no longer sent correctly: tick the right columns again (Edit), or check the document’s access rules.
send.export.rowsGone: This export’s rows are gone from the Synchro table (deleted by hand in Grist?): nothing is sent any more. Click “Edit” to choose the tables and columns again. The recipients’ signing keys were in those rows: see each person’s notice.
send.vanished: {n} {n|recipient you added is|recipients you added are} no longer listed: {n|the webhook was deleted|their webhooks were deleted} or changed by hand in Grist’s settings (Document settings, API). {n|This person receives|These people receive} nothing more from this export: invite {n|them|them} again (Add a recipient).
send.delete.title: Delete the export “{name}”?
send.delete.body: Deliveries stop for {n} {n|recipient|recipients}. What they already received stays with them. The id_sync and MajLe columns stay in your tables.
send.person.title: Add a recipient to “{name}”
send.person.badAddress: This recipient’s sending address was changed in Grist’s settings: it is no longer a form address on this instance. Revoke it if there is no explanation.
send.person.noKey: This person’s signing key was lost (the “signature” row of the Synchro table deleted?): their document rejects your sends as suspect. The key cannot be remade: revoke them, then invite them again (their reception resumes).
send.person.otherDoc: This recipient now sends to another document ({doc}) than the one approved. Revoke it if there is no explanation.
send.mode.reply: One way (recommended): your changes go to the recipient, who sends you back a reply code
send.mode.public: Public link: a single code, the recipient reads the export without replying (publishable data)
send.mode.publicDone: Public link: already open for this export (Code button on its card)
send.mode.publicStrong: Public link: not possible for an export with enhanced security
send.mode.echange: Both ways (Exchange): their changes also come back here, the most recent one wins
send.mode.echange.more: One more participant in the Exchange (multi-party Exchange)
send.mode.echange.moreHelp: This document runs the Exchange: it receives each participant’s changes and passes them on to the others, the most recent one winning. Participants do not know each other: each one is only connected to this document. A row ticked Supprime by a participant stays here, ticked, and disappears for the others.
send.mode.echange.help: Both documents keep each other up to date. Deleting a row only deletes it on one side: tick its Supprime box to delete it on both. The recipient must own their document. Other participants can join later: this document then runs the Exchange.
send.mode.echange.off: Both ways (Exchange): only for an export with no recipient nor invitation, and no public link
send.back.title: Return form link
send.back.help: The recipient’s changes will arrive here through a return form, published {where}. Copy its link and paste it here: it goes into the invitation, and only the recipient can use it.
send.exchange.managed: Exchange received from another document: it is managed from the Receive tab. Deleting it stops the Exchange.
send.exchange.with: Exchange: this recipient’s changes come back into your tables.
send.exchange.hub: Multi-party Exchange ({n} participants): each one’s changes come back to your tables and go on to the others.
send.rules.title: Changes received from participants
send.rules.help: For each kind of change: accept it, refuse it, or keep it for review on the participant’s card, in the Receive tab.
send.refusal.title: When a change is refused
send.refusal.corriger: The participant takes back this document’s row (recommended)
send.refusal.signaler: The participant keeps their version, the difference is flagged here
send.refusal.help: Taking back this document’s row deletes a refused addition on their side (the row stays here, with Supprime ticked) and brings back a row whose deletion is refused.
send.public.warn: The widget adds access rules: anyone who is only a viewer of the document (including the public link) will only see the public exports, nothing else. Then, in Share, Manage users, set “Public access” to On, as Viewer. Avoid for data that must not be public.
send.public.columns: Anyone with the document link will be able to read these columns: {list}.
send.public.editors: This document’s public link is set to Editor: anyone can change it, and the widget’s rules no longer protect anything. In Share, Manage users, set “Public access” back to Viewer.
send.public.hiddenNow: An access rule now hides part of {tables}, which this public link shows to everyone. Turn off the public link, or remove these tables from the export.
send.public.label: public link
send.public.turnOn: To do: in the document Share menu, Manage users: “Public access” On, as Viewer, then Confirm.
send.public.help: Send this code: it is all the recipient needs. It holds no data.
send.public.revokeBody: Viewers will no longer see this export. Also turn off the public link in Share if it is no longer used: while it stays on, the widget keeps the rule that hides the rest of the document.
send.public.tooBig: Too large for the public link (over 2 MB): {tables}. The public link gives nothing of it; invite the person instead (webhook), or filter the rows.
send.check.missing: When creating the export, the widget will add: {items}.
send.check.sync: the Synchro technical table (one for all exports)
send.renforce.help: The control code must be compared with the person before connecting, the deletions they receive always need approval, and this export can no longer be shared by public link.
send.renforce.structure: Enhanced security: editors of this document can change its structure, hence the formulas that choose what is sent. Untick “Allow editors to edit structure” in the access rules.
send.invite.help: Give this code to the person managing the TARGET document. They paste it in this widget, “Receive” tab, then send you back a reply code.
send.invite.expiredOn: Expired on {at}: make a new code
send.invite.expired: This invitation has expired: go back to make a new code.
send.invite.backCode: Control code of the return feed:
send.reply.title: Recipient’s reply
send.reply.help: Paste the reply code received from the TARGET document.
send.reply.nosecret: This invitation has no secret, so check the details before approving.
send.reply.verified: Document, folder and team come from Grist; the email and date come from the pasted code.
send.reply.personal: This document is in a personal space: Grist does not say who owns it. Check by phone with the person, using the control code.
send.reply.compared: I compared this code with the person: it is the same.
send.load.body: Connecting only sends future changes. Send {n} {n|existing row|existing rows} now?
send.load.empty: The tables are empty for now: rows will go out as soon as they are added.
send.load.done: Resend finished: {n} {n|row|rows} sent. At the recipient they show up as soon as their widget page is open.
send.load.queued: Another resend is running for this document (another page or another person): this one is noted, and will leave by itself afterwards, while a widget page stays open.
send.load.nobody: No connected recipient: nothing to resend.
send.load.nothing: None of the table’s {n} {n|row|rows} can go out: they lack the sync key, or the export’s filter leaves them all out.
send.estimate.title: Long send
send.estimate.body: {rows} {rows|row|rows} to send, about {size}, in {lots} {lots|batch|batches}, for {n} {n|recipient|recipients}: allow {dur}.
send.estimate.pace: To spare Grist’s server, the widget sends no more than {mb} MB every {min} minutes, all recipients combined. Keep a widget page open until the end: progress shows on the export’s card.
send.flow.runningOther: A send is running from another page or another person: {done} of {total} {total|row|rows} ({pct}%), batch {lot} of about {lots}. It carries on by itself.
send.flow.budget: Paused to spare Grist’s server: the rest leaves around {at} ({done} of {total} {total|row|rows} already sent, {pct}%). Nothing is lost; keep a widget page open.
send.flow.budgetWait: Sends spaced out to spare Grist’s server: the rest leaves around {at}. Ordinary changes always leave.
send.flow.queued: Another send is running for this document: this one leaves afterwards, by itself.
send.flow.paused: {n} {n|table still has|tables still have} rows to send, but no recipient is active: they leave when sending resumes.
send.flow.blocked: Sending is blocked: {n} {n|recipient is|recipients are} failing (see below). Until that is fixed nothing is resent, because Grist’s delivery queue is shared by all recipients.
send.flow.interrupted: Send interrupted at {done} of {total} {total|row|rows} ({pct}%): it resumes by itself as soon as an owner has the widget page open.
send.flow.waiting: Waiting: {n} {n|table|tables} to complete. The widget sends them by itself, every 10 seconds, while a widget page stays open.
send.load.background: You can close this window: sending carries on while the page stays open, and otherwise resumes the next time an owner opens the widget.
send.cancel.title: Withdraw this invitation?
send.cancel.body: Its code can no longer be accepted.
send.resume.title: Resume “{name}”
send.resume.catchup: Catch up on changes made during the pause (recommended)
send.resume.catchup.help: Sends {n} {n|row|rows} added or changed during the pause, and the deletions. The rest of the table is not sent again.
send.resume.all: The pause time is unknown, or the columns changed during the pause: the whole export is sent.
send.resume.asIs.help: Only future changes are sent. Rows added, changed or deleted during the pause will not reach the TARGET unless they change again (or with “Resend all”).
send.revoke.title: Revoke “{name}”?
send.revoke.body: Deliveries stop for this person only; other recipients go on. What they already received stays with them.
send.revoke.exchange: The Exchange stops: your changes no longer go out, theirs no longer come back (the return log is deleted). Tables keep their rows, on both sides.
send.revoke.participant: This participant no longer receives anything and their changes no longer come back (their return log is deleted). The other participants carry on. Tables keep their rows.
send.unblock.title: Unblock the delivery queue?
send.unblock.body: The delivery queue is shared by the whole document: its pending deliveries are dropped, then the widget resends the exports on its own (keep this page open). If someone no longer receives, revoke or pause them first, or the queue will get stuck again.
send.unsafe.title: Unfiltered delivery
send.unsafe.body: These deliveries (Grist webhooks) read the Synchro table without an export filter: they would receive every export. Delete them: {who}.
send.unsafe.confirm: These deliveries are deleted from Grist. Their recipients no longer receive anything.
send.stray.title: Extra columns in the Synchro table
send.stray.body: The Synchro table belongs to the widget: it should only have its {total} columns. The widget finds {n} extra {n|column|columns}: {list}. {n|It does|They do} not come from the widget: Grist adds columns A, B and C to every new table, and a Synchro table made before the widget may have kept them. Every delivery carries the whole Synchro row, and the recipient’s journal refuses a column it does not know (“Invalid column”): while {n|it is|they are} there, deliveries fail.
send.stray.filled: Holds values or a formula: {cols}. Save them before removing.
send.stray.dialog.title: Remove the extra columns?
send.stray.dialog.intro: {n|This column will be removed|These columns will be removed} from the Synchro table. The widget’s columns, your exports and your recipients do not change.
send.stray.empty: {n|It is empty|They are empty}: nothing will be lost.
send.stray.save: {n|This column holds|These columns hold} values or a formula ({cols}), and removing {n|it erases it|them erases them}. Before going on, save {n|it|them}: copy the values to another table of the document, or to a file.
send.stray.sure: I have saved what needed keeping
send.stray.unblock: Deliveries are blocked because of these columns. After the removal, the widget empties Grist’s delivery queue (its waiting deliveries, which still carry the columns, are dropped), then resends the exports by itself. Keep this page open.
send.keys.title: Some rows will not reach the recipients
send.keys.help: Every row has a key (id_sync column) that identifies it on their side. A row without a key is not sent; two rows with the same key become a single row on their side, and the other never arrives. This happens when whole rows are duplicated or pasted, or when cells of this column are cleared.
send.keys.line: Table {table}: {blank} {blank|row without a key|rows without a key}, {dup} {dup|row sharing|rows sharing} the key of another.
send.keys.missing: Table {table}: {n|column deleted|columns deleted} ({cols}). These columns come from the widget; without them, changes to this table no longer go out.
send.keys.dialog.missing: The widget puts back the columns it had added and that were deleted. If id_sync was missing, every row gets a fresh key: for the recipients, the rows already received are replaced by these new rows (a large deletion waits for their approval).
send.keys.dialog.title: Repair the keys
send.keys.dialog.body: The widget gives a new key to {n} {n|row|rows} (id_sync column only; the oldest row of each group keeps its own), then sends them as after an edit. On the recipients’ side, duplicated rows become separate rows. No other value in your table is changed.
send.error.stray: This person no longer receives because of the column “{col}” of this document’s Synchro table, which does not belong to the widget: nothing to do on their side. Remove the extra columns (card at the top of the tab); delivery then resumes.
send.error.gone: The column “{col}” is no longer in the Synchro table, but Grist’s delivery queue still holds old deliveries that carry it. “Unblock the queue” drops them: the widget then resends the exports by itself.
send.foreign.title: A table named Synchro already exists
send.foreign.body: The widget needs its own table named Synchro, and does not take over someone else’s: it would add its columns, and every delivery would carry yours too, which recipients refuse.
send.foreign.how: Rename it to free the name: it keeps its columns, values and formulas, only its name changes. The widget then creates its own table at the first export.
send.foreign.name: New name for your table
send.foreign.done: Table renamed. The widget creates its own Synchro table at the first export.
send.foreign.blocked: A table named Synchro already exists: rename it first.
send.lost.deleted.title: The Synchro table was deleted
send.lost.deleted.body: This table is the widget’s memory: your list of exports and the recipients’ signing keys were in it. Without it nothing is sent any more. Grist still keeps {n} {n|webhook|webhooks} of the former recipients, which are now useless.
send.lost.deleted.how: If the deletion is recent, undo it: Ctrl+Z in Grist, or “Document history” (in the tools, on the left) to get an earlier version back. Otherwise remove the old webhooks, create your exports again and invite each person again: signing keys are made again at the invitation.
send.lost.deleted.confirm: The {n} {n|webhook|webhooks} of the former Synchro table will be deleted. Nothing is erased at the recipients: they keep the rows already received, but receive nothing more until you invite them again.
send.lost.deleted.done: {n} {n|old webhook removed|old webhooks removed}. You can create a new export.
send.lost.renamed.title: The Synchro table was renamed
send.lost.renamed.body: The widget looks for it under the name Synchro, and it is now called “{name}”: nothing is sent to the recipients any more, and your list of exports does not show.
send.lost.renamed.how: Give it the name Synchro back (in “Raw data”, click the table’s name): everything resumes, nothing is lost.
send.lost.hidden.title: The widget can no longer read the Synchro table
send.lost.hidden.body: The Synchro table is there, but the widget no longer finds its Synchro_Export column: it was deleted, or an access rule hides the table or this column, owners included. Nothing is sent as long as this lasts.
send.lost.hidden.how: Open “Access rules” (in the tools, on the left) and remove the rule that hides the Synchro table or this column. If the column was deleted, Ctrl+Z or “Document history” brings it back.
send.lost.blocked: The widget’s Synchro table is lost: fix that first.
send.error.size: Delivery too big for Grist (over 1 MB): the widget clears the queue and resends everything on its own. Keep this page open.
send.error.column: This person’s journal does not have the column “{col}” that the widget sends: ask them to open their widget page, which updates their journal. Delivery then resumes on its own.
send.error.link: This person’s receiving link no longer works (their document was deleted, the reception stopped, the link cut or the form unpublished: Grist answers the same in all four cases). While this lasts, deliveries to the other people of this document wait behind this one: pause them to free those, then revoke them and invite them again.
send.error.journal: This person’s receiving journal was deleted in their document: the link still exists, but there is no table left to write to. While this lasts, sends to the other people of this document wait behind this one: pause this person to free them, then revoke them and invite them again (they then set up their reception again).
send.behind: {n} {n|recipient is|recipients are} waiting behind the failing delivery to {who}: Grist’s delivery queue is shared by the whole document. Their deliveries will resume as soon as that person is paused or revoked, or their delivery succeeds.
send.error.rate: This person’s server limits the number of deliveries (error 429). Grist retries on its own for about a quarter of an hour: nothing to do if it recovers. Meanwhile, deliveries to the other people of this document wait behind this one; pause them to free those.
send.error.server: This person’s server answered with an error on its side (error {status}). Grist retries on its own for about a quarter of an hour: nothing to do if it recovers. Meanwhile, deliveries to the other people of this document wait behind this one; pause them to free those.
send.error.network: This person’s server could not be reached (connection refused or cut). Grist retries on its own for about a quarter of an hour. If it lasts, check with them that their document still exists. Meanwhile, deliveries to the other people of this document wait behind this one; pause them to free those.
send.error.slow: This person’s server does not answer: a delivery has been waiting for its answer for more than three minutes (Grist gives up after five minutes, then retries). Deliveries to the other people of this document wait behind this one; pause them to free those.
send.error.other: This person no longer receives: while the delivery fails, the document’s delivery queue is blocked for everyone.
recv.empty: No export received. Paste an invitation received from the SOURCE document.
recv.emptyViewer: No visible reception: this document’s journals may be reserved to its editors.
recv.invite.title: Invitation received
recv.invite.help: Paste the invitation code sent by the SOURCE document.
recv.dest: Where to store each received table: a new table, or a table of this document.
recv.backDoc: Your changes will go back to the document {doc} (checked by Grist).
recv.backPersonal: This document is in a personal space: Grist does not say who owns it. Check by phone with the person who invited you.
recv.backCode: Control code of the return feed:
recv.backCompared: I compared this code with the person who invited me: it is the same.
recv.renforce: Enhanced security: received deletions will need approval here.
recv.reserve: Reception journal readable by editors only (recommended): it keeps the received versions, whatever the access rules of the destination tables.
recv.reserve.owner: This journal will be restricted to editors when an owner of the document opens this page.
recv.archive: Archive: keep a row deleted at the SOURCE. It stays in the table, ticked “Deleted at the source”, and is no longer followed. For a right to erasure, it is up to you to delete it.
recv.lock: Received tables are read-only: only the document owners can write in them (the widget copies when one of them opens this page).
recv.lock.ownerOnly: Only a document owner can change this setting.
recv.lock.limit: This protects against edits by hand, not against an editor who would change the reception journal or the document structure.
recv.archive.off: Unticking the archive does not delete the rows already archived: they stay ticked.
recv.lock.waiting: Read-only: copying waits for an owner to open this page.
recv.options.title: Options of “{name}”
recv.history.none: No change since your last visit.
recv.history.rowGone: Row {n} of the table, before it was deleted
recv.drift.title: {dest}: {n} {n|change|changes} made by hand here
recv.drift.body: {n|It stays|They stay} until the SOURCE changes the same row. “Fix” puts the exact SOURCE state back now.
recv.wave.title: {dest}: the SOURCE deleted {n} {n|row|rows}
recv.wave.body: Many rows at once: nothing is deleted here before your decision. Check with the SOURCE whether this is intended.
recv.wave.strict: Enhanced security: nothing is deleted here before your decision.
recv.wave.applyBody: {n|The row disappears|The rows disappear} from this document, as in the SOURCE.
recv.wave.ignoreBody: {n|The row stays|The rows stay} here, detached from the SOURCE: nothing updates or deletes {n|it|them} any more.
recv.drift.fixTitle: Put the SOURCE values back in {dest}?
recv.drift.fixBody: {n} {n|change made by hand here is replaced|changes made by hand here are replaced} by the exact SOURCE state.
recv.drift.fixRows: {n} {n|row deleted here comes|rows deleted here come} back, at the end of the table.
recv.drift.fixCols: {n} {n|column deleted here is|columns deleted here are} created again.
recv.drift.rowGone: Row deleted here, still in the SOURCE
recv.drift.colGone: Column deleted here, still sent by the SOURCE
recv.review.title: {dest}: {n} {n|change|changes} to review
recv.review.body: Sent by this participant, they await your decision: nothing is written here or passed on to the other participants before.
recv.review.accepterAllBody: {n} {n|change to review is copied|changes to review are copied} here.
recv.review.refuserAllBody: {n} {n|change to review is refused|changes to review are refused}.
recv.gap.title: {dest}: {n} refused {n|row is|rows are} still different for the participant
recv.gap.body: They keep their version (export setting). The difference goes away at the next change of the row, here or on their side.
recv.gap.ajout: Added on their side, not here
recv.gap.suppression: Deleted on their side, kept here
recv.label.title: Displayed column
recv.label.help: Column that names each row in the history, per table.
recv.existing: Choose the column receiving each sent column. The widget adds new columns and a hidden id_sync key.
recv.dest.name: Name of the new table for {table}
recv.undo.title: Back to the destinations?
recv.undo.body: This reception’s journal and its form are deleted, with its write link; so are the tables it created, if they are still empty. You will choose again where to store each table.
recv.match.help: An existing row whose value in this column equals a received row is updated instead of duplicated. Other existing rows are never touched.
recv.link.title: Form link
recv.link.help: A receiving form was just published {where}. Copy its link and paste it here: it works for every table of the export.
recv.link.step1: 1. Open the form’s page and click “Share” in its card.
recv.link.step2: 2. Click “Copy link”, then paste it below.
recv.link.where: on its own page, at the bottom of the page list
recv.link.where.page: on page “{page}”, in the page list (open it)
recv.reply.help: Send this code back to the person who invited you: they paste it in their widget to connect the feed.
recv.ended: The SOURCE cut this feed on {at} (revoked, export deleted or Exchange stopped): nothing more will arrive. Tables keep their rows; “Stop receiving” removes the journal and its form.
recv.unsigned: Reception from before signed deliveries: whoever gets the form link can write to it. Ask the SOURCE for a new invitation: the same reception resumes, protected.
recv.formGone: The receiving form is no longer published (unpublished or page deleted): the SOURCE can no longer write here, so nothing arrives. “Redo the link” publishes it again; the SOURCE must then revoke this reception and invite you again.
recv.sync.none: Nothing new: everything is up to date.
recv.consent: If you continue, the widget creates in this document the new destination tables (or adds their columns and a hidden id_sync key to existing tables), a technical journal for this export, and its receiving form, on its own page.
recv.consent.public: If you continue, the widget creates in this document the new destination tables (or adds their columns and a hidden id_sync key to existing tables) and a technical journal without a page for this export.
recv.consent.echange: Exchange: your changes to these tables will go back to the SOURCE document, the most recent one winning; it may pass them on to other participants of the Exchange. The widget adds the MajLe and RecalculLe columns to the destination tables and creates a return export (Send tab). Deleting a row only deletes it here: tick its Supprime box to delete it everywhere.
recv.outgoing.title: Send these columns?
recv.outgoing.body: In an Exchange, an existing table goes back in full to the other document: the columns {list} will go to {where}, and their changes will follow.
recv.exchange: Exchange: your changes to these tables go back to that document, which may pass them on to other participants.
recv.exchange.back: Exchange: this participant’s changes come into your tables, following the export’s rules (Send tab).
recv.public: Public link: read again while this page is open, only when the export changes.
recv.public.done: Connected: the widget reads the SOURCE while this page is open.
recv.stop.title: Stop receiving “{name}”?
recv.stop.body: The widget deletes the journal {journal} and its receiving form, with its write link: the SOURCE deliveries will fail and it will have to revoke. Destination tables and their rows stay.
recv.auto: Updated automatically while this page is open: every 10 seconds, every minute when nothing arrives.
recv.missing: {table}: {n} {n|row has|rows have} not arrived yet (sent in several parts). {n|It is sent|They are sent} on {n|its|their} own while an owner of the SOURCE keeps its widget page open: if this number does not go down, ask them to open it.
recv.arrival: Last delivery arrived: {at} · {n} {n|row|rows} in the journal.
recv.arrival.raw: {n} {n|delivery that arrived is|deliveries that arrived are} not copied into the tables yet: the widget does it while this page stays open and visible.
recv.action.report: Copy the status for the SOURCE
recv.report.copied: Status copied. Paste it in a message to the person who sends: it holds no code, no link and no value from your tables.
recv.report.failed: Copy is not possible from here: select and copy the text below.
recv.tally: {table}: the SOURCE announces {expected} {expected|row|rows}, but only {got} arrived here, and nothing has changed for {min} minutes. {gap} {gap|row is|rows are} missing. A delivery may have been lost (Grist restarted, delivery queue cleared), or some SOURCE rows share the same key. Ask an owner of the SOURCE to open its widget page and click “Resend all”; “Copy the status for the SOURCE” gives them what they need to check.
recv.big: {table}: {n} {n|row|rows} cannot arrive, each larger than the maximum size of a Grist send (1 MB). Shorten it in the SOURCE.
recv.tooBig: {tables}: too large for the public link (over 2 MB), nothing of it is read. Ask the SOURCE for an invitation, or a row filter.
recv.files.waiting: {n} {n|file|files} expected in {dest}: {n|it arrives|they arrive} when an owner of the SOURCE document opens the widget page.
recv.files.big: Too big to be sent ({max} MB at most): {files}.
recv.files.public: Attachments do not travel through the public link: their columns stay empty in {dest}.
recv.files.refused: Grist refuses to store the file {name} here ({error}): next try in 10 minutes.
recv.suspect.title: Suspicious arrivals
recv.suspect.rejected: {n} {n|row|rows} rejected in the journal, {n|on|the last on} {at}: {n|it|they} could not come from this export’s SOURCE (other export, unreadable content). Nothing was copied.
recv.suspect.flood: Abnormal arrival on {at}: more than 600 rows in a minute, processed in small batches.
recv.suspect.help: Two possible explanations. Either the SOURCE document was edited by hand (a column, formula or table deleted): ask whoever manages it to look at the Send tab of their widget, which flags it. Or someone other than the SOURCE writes with the form link: if you cannot explain it, cut the link.
recv.cut.title: Cut the form link?
recv.cut.body: The old link will write nothing more into this reception, and the SOURCE’s sends will fail. To resume, the SOURCE revokes the old recipient and sends you a new invitation: accept it here, the same reception resumes with its tables and a new form, on its own page.
recv.cut.done: Link cut. Ask the SOURCE for a new invitation, and accept it here.
recv.shared.title: Link shared with other forms
recv.shared.body: This reception’s form is on a page holding {n} other {n|form|forms}: their shared link can also write into this journal. Cut the link: this reception will resume with its own form, on its own page.
recv.relink: This export is already received here: the same reception resumes with this new invitation. Copy the form link (it may have changed).
recv.relink.confirm: “{name}” is already received in this document (journal {journal}). This invitation resumes the same reception, with its tables: check that it comes from the same person and the same document.
recv.offer.title: Table added to the export: {table}
recv.offer.refuseBody: Its rows will be deleted on arrival, now and later. To receive it afterwards, you will have to stop receiving and accept a new invitation.
recv.offer.where: Table receiving the rows (new or existing)
recv.offer.refusedList: Refused tables (their rows are deleted on arrival): {tables}.
error.codeFormat: This text is not a sync code. Copy the whole code, from “GRISTSYNC2.” to the end.
error.codeOld: This code comes from a previous version of the widget. Ask for a new invitation.
error.codeNewer: This code comes from version {theirs} of the widget, newer than the one in this document ({mine}). Both documents must use the widget from the same address: check it in the widget settings (Grist’s right panel), reload the page, then paste the code again.
error.inviteOld: This reply comes from an invitation made by a previous version of the widget. Make a new code (“Back”, then “Make a new code”) and send the new one.
error.notInvitation: This code is a reply, not an invitation.
error.notReply: This code is an invitation, not a reply.
error.codeInvalid: This code is incomplete or altered.
error.otherInstance: The TARGET document is on another Grist instance: sending is refused.
error.alreadyReceived: This export is already received in this document, through a public link or from another document: stop that reception first.
error.exportTaken: This invitation reuses the identifier of an export of this document: it would replace it. It does not come from an up-to-date widget, or was modified: refuse it.
error.unknownInvitation: This reply matches no pending invitation of this document, or its secret differs.
error.invitationExpired: This invitation has expired (it is valid for 7 days). Ask the person who sent it for a new one, or make a new code.
error.shareUnreadable: Grist does not answer to check this link’s document. Try again in a moment.
error.shareUnknown: This link leads to no published form: it was cut, or copied incomplete.
error.shareOtherDoc: Refused: this link writes to another document than the one the code says. Do not connect, and warn the person.
error.codeNotCompared: Enhanced security: first compare the control code with the person, then tick the box.
error.publicHidden: Public link refused: an access rule hides part of {tables}. The public link would show it to everyone; remove these columns or tables from the export, or invite the person instead.
error.publicHiddenEdit: Change refused: this export is shared by public link, and an access rule hides part of {tables}. The public link would show it to everyone; remove these tables from the export, or turn off the public link first.
error.mapTwice: Two sent columns go to the same column.
error.matchUnmapped: The attach column must receive a sent column.
error.publicClosed: The SOURCE document can no longer be read by public link.
error.noColumn: Tick at least one column per table.
error.loop: Loop refused: a received table cannot be sent back to the document it comes from, nor a table to itself. That would be a two-way sync. Relaying to another document is fine.
error.destTaken: {dest} already receives the table {table}: a table here receives only one sent table. Choose a new table, or another existing table.
error.destTwice: Two received tables go to {dest}: a table here receives only one sent table. Choose another destination for one of them.
error.destReserved: {dest} is a name reserved for the widget: choose another one.
error.destExported: This document already sends this table in an export: it cannot also receive one (its rows would be deleted). Choose another table.
error.ownerOnly: Only a document owner can do this.
error.keyLost: signing key not found (destination table or id_sync column deleted?), nothing is copied. Ask the SOURCE for a new invitation: the same reception resumes.
error.gristTooOld: This Grist instance cannot filter a webhook by export (Grist 1.7.11 or later is needed). Nothing was connected.
error.queueStuck: The delivery queue does not empty: a recipient no longer receives. See the error on its line, then try again.
error.tableNameInvalid: The name can only have letters without accents, digits and “_”, and does not start with a digit.
error.tableNameTaken: A table of this document already has that name.
error.syncTableForeign: A table named Synchro already exists in this document, and the widget does not take over someone else’s: the Send tab offers to rename it. Do so, then try again.
error.tooLarge: A delivery exceeds the size Grist allows (1 MB). The widget clears the queue and resends everything on its own: keep this page open.
error.formLink: This link does not have the expected form: https://<instance>/o/<team>/forms/<key>/<number>.
error.exchangeOwner: An Exchange also creates a sending from this document: you must own it.
error.linkTest: The link does not work ({detail}). Check that the form is published and the document is in a team site.
error.linkElsewhere: This link does not write into this reception’s journal (another reception’s form, or another document’s). Copy the link of the form named above.
error.blockedRules: An access rule of this document stops the widget from writing here ({detail}). In Grist: Document settings, Access rules; remove or relax the rule that applies to this table. The widget’s tables (Synchro, journals) and the received tables must stay editable by the people who use them.
start.outside: This widget opens inside Grist: add a custom widget, custom URL, paste the address below and choose full access.
start.access: The widget needs full access to the document: it reads its tables, creates its technical table and writes to the destination tables. Without it, it stays stuck on this message.
start.access.where: The setting is in Grist’s right panel, “Access level” section. First click this widget, then:
start.access.open: Panel closed: click the framed icon, at the very top right, to open it
start.access.list: Or pick “Full document access” in the list
start.slow: Grist does not answer the widget. Check that it has full access to the document (right panel: “Accept”, or “Full document access” under “Access level”), then reload the page. If it lasts, check your connection.
start.network: The widget cannot load the Grist API from {origin}: the network blocks it, or this instance is not in the widget’s list.
start.failed: The widget could not read the document. {detail} Reload the page.
